description: Configuration for the iceberg forecast uncertainty cone (src/models/iceberg_uncertainty.py). The radius is CALIBRATED from the empirical radial endpoint errors of the frozen physics baseline at 24 h. Its growth to other horizons is a PROJECT ASSUMPTION, not a measured law.

calibration.population: clean 24 h observed->observed MOVED rows with both environmental inputs
calibration.split_note: the chronological split established for the residual experiment is reused verbatim so the held-out test rows are the same ones, and the uncertainty layer never sees them during calibration

growth.assumption_statement: The square-root exponent of 0.5 is the growth a random-walk displacement error would follow. It is ASSUMED here, not fitted: this project has exactly one empirically calibrated horizon (24 h), and the 6 clean moved 48 h rows available cannot distinguish sqrt growth from linear growth or from anything else. The linear law is provided for sensitivity testing only and MUST NOT be selected using the 48 h data.
growth.law_selection_forbidden_on: the 48 h rows, and any test-split row

secondary_component_statistics.note: east/north spread and their correlation are recorded so a later step can decide whether an ellipse is worth the complexity. The PRIMARY and only supported output of this layer is a circular radius, because that is what the collision-risk visualisation consumes.

known_limitations: 24 h is the ONLY empirically calibrated horizon. Every other horizon, shorter or longer, is produced by the assumed growth law and carries no direct evidence.
Horizons beyond 24 h are flagged extrapolated_uncertainty = true. 48 h is supported arithmetically and is NOT empirically validated.
The calibration population is ASCAT-only: every clean moved 24 h row in this dataset comes from that sensor, so the radius describes ASCAT-derived tracks.
The radius is calibrated against the FROZEN physics baseline (windage 0.0, turn 0.0). If the physics configuration changes, this calibration is void and must be re-run.
The cone is circular by design. The secondary component statistics record whether east and north errors actually differ enough for that to matter.

Errors are radial great-circle distances between the predicted and observed endpoint; they fold together environmental error, the constant-velocity assumption and the position uncertainty of the source chart, and cannot separate them.
not_included: any change to the physics model
